definition: Expected technical service life of the installed equipment.
Rated (nameplate) capacity of one unit: the most it can make running flat out, on the basis named in capacity-basis. A rate, not what the unit makes; see annual-output.
optimization-use: Unit size for integer or lumpy investment; otherwise the cost denominator.

definition: Annual output as a fraction of output at rated capacity running continuously.
Useful output of one unit over a typical year: capacity x capacity-factor. In the database's units, MW x 31,536 GJ/yr per MW, or kt/yr x 1000 t per kt, times the capacity factor.

Useful output per unit of energy input, on a higher heating value (HHV) basis: a source's LHV figure is converted with the heating values of the fuel in and the product out (pipeline/heating.py). For multi-carrier technologies record one tech-flow row per input instead.
optimization-use: Inverted to an input coefficient in the activity matrix.

definition: Combined heat and electricity output per unit of fuel input.
Useful heat output per unit of electricity output for a CHP unit.
Total final energy input per unit of product output, all carriers, on a final-energy basis.
optimization-use: Benchmark for calibrating the activity matrix.

definition: Feedstock whose energy ends in the product (gas into hydrogen, ammonia, or methanol; biomass or oil into fuels; naphtha into HVC), GJ HHV per unit of product, by carrier in target. Not part of specific-energy-consumption (ruling 2026-10-13).
optimization-use: The feed the technology requests besides its energy use.

definition: Temperature of the heat an archetype meant to supply heat delivers (steam, hot water, hot gas or thermal oil): heat supply, boilers, and archetypes with heat or steam among their products. Not a heating surface or a turbine exhaust.
Low end where the source gives a range; rolled into the low of heat-output-temp.
High end where the source gives a range; rolled into the high of heat-output-temp.

Temperature the process needs to achieve its end use (kiln sintering, bath, reactor, cooking or drying temperature); not the temperature of the heating side (flame, flue gas, heating surface, tube wall, steam or hot gas supplied). Sets heat-process-tier where it exists.
Low end where the source gives a range; rolled into the low of heat-process-temp.
High end where the source gives a range; rolled into the high of heat-process-temp.

Temperature of a heat stream leaving the archetype that waste-heat recovery could use (exhaust, flue gas, stack gas, exhaust air, engine coolant, condenser heat); every stream pooled as one, the stream named in the example row.
Low end where the source gives a range; rolled into the low of heat-waste-temp.
High end where the source gives a range; rolled into the high of heat-waste-temp.
Pressure of delivered steam. Record the source's own unit.

Percentage of the hours in a year the unit is ABLE to run, after planned and unplanned outages. It is a property of the equipment, not of how it is operated: capacity-factor is what it actually produced, and is bounded above by this. A boiler at 90% availability and a 60% capacity factor was available for 90% of the year and run for 60% of it.
optimization-use: Upper bound on annual activity, separate from the dispatch decision.

definition: Lowest sustained output as a fraction of rated capacity.
optimization-use: Lower bound on operation when committed.

definition: Annual fractional loss of efficiency or capacity over the lifetime.
Overnight capital cost per unit of capacity, on the basis named in cost-basis.
Annual operating and maintenance cost that does not vary with output.
Operating cost per unit of output, excluding purchased energy and feedstock.

Fixed and variable operating cost reported TOGETHER, where the source does not split them. Say in the row note exactly what it includes - sources differ on whether fuel, electricity, materials, and depreciation are inside. Never record an opex-fixed or opex-variable on top of an opex-total for the same technology and source.

Cost per unit of product or service including capital recovery, as the source reports it: a levelized cost of electricity, heat, hydrogen, or product, a production cost, or a cost per tonne of CO2 captured, transported, or stored. NOT a capex or opex and never pooled with one; it depends on the source's discount rate, fuel prices, and capacity factor, which its note records (discount-rate is recorded as its own parameter where printed). Added 2026-09-25; loaded from main files and from the sidecars that held levelized costs, 2026-09-26.
note: Normalised to 2025_CAD per unit of the archetype product. A levelized cost the source states as an adder on a base plant carries cost-basis incremental and is set aside like other incremental costs.

definition: Annualization factor applied to capex. Record the source study's own factor, not the model's.
Financial rate used by the source when levelizing. Recorded so a levelized cost can be inverted without double-counting the model's own hurdle rate.
Years from investment decision to commissioning.
Fractional capex reduction per doubling of cumulative installed capacity.
End-of-life cost per unit of capacity.

Emissions from burning fuel at the technology, per unit of energy input or product output. Species named in target. Excludes the process reaction, which is emissions-process, and excludes purchased energy, which is out of scope.
Emissions from the chemical reaction rather than fuel combustion, per unit of product.

Combustion plus process emissions together, per unit of product, where a source reports only the combined figure. Scope 1. NEVER record this alongside emissions-combustion and emissions-process for the same technology and source - it is the sum of them, and the three together double count.

Biogenic CO2 released at the technology per unit of product: from biomass fuels (black liquor, wood, biogas) or carbonate whose carbon came from biomass (kraft lime mud). Not part of emissions-combustion, emissions-process, or emissions-total, which are fossil (ruling 2026-10-14).
Emissions captured rather than released, per unit of energy input or product output. Species named in target. The counterpart of capture-rate as an absolute quantity.

Fraction of the CO2 entering the capture plant that it captures. Recorded on capture plants (the co2-capture family) only. The plant-level capture rate is share-to-capture on the host times this, and is not recorded directly.
note: Redefined 2026-10-02 (modeller): capture-plant side only; a source's plant-level rate on a host is recorded as share-to-capture.

parameter-label: Share of CO2 sent to capture
definition: Fraction of the host plant's CO2 sent to the capture plant. Recorded on host plants with capture. Times the capture plant's capture-rate it gives the plant-level capture rate; where a source gives only the plant-level rate, that rate is recorded here.
optimization-use: With the host's CO2 per unit of product, sets the service request to the capture service.

definition: Cost of avoiding one tonne of CO2-eq by using this technology instead of the incumbent, as the source reports it. NOT a capital or operating cost and never interchangeable with one: it already nets the technology's costs against the incumbent's and divides by the emissions avoided, so the incumbent it was measured against belongs in the note. Added 2026-08-29 for IPCC AR6 Chapter 11 Table 11.3, which reports costs only in this form.
optimization-use: A marginal abatement cost curve point; not a substitute for capex and opex.

definition: Reduction in GHG emissions this option can deliver relative to current practice, as a percentage. A ceiling on what the option can do, not a projection of what it will do. Where a source says these are multiplicative rather than additive across options -- as IPCC AR6 Table 11.3 does -- they must not be summed.
optimization-use: Bounds the share of a service this option can decarbonize.

definition: Earliest year the technology may be built. From the TRL rule (design doc D5) where pre-commercial; a region-specific override goes here, the default on the technology row.
Year after which the technology may no longer be built.
